typefully-a.verdict: The only page where every face has one job and keeps to it, with the best-set headline of the five.
typefully-a.loved: The H1: Newsreader 380 at 118px with automatic optical sizing, a grey 'Make it', and the italic 'hookworthy.' dropped to weight 360 so its colour matches the roman. That is real type direction. The roles are strict: your draft is in serif, the X preview is in Inter like the real network, and Geist Mono is used only for times and counts. The wordmark (Inter bold 'hook' plus Newsreader italic 'worthy') sums up the pairing.
problems: The phone scale is flat. The H1 is 42.9px and every H2 is 39px (a ratio of 1.10), so on a phone the headline barely outranks a section title.
H3s keep switching family: Inter 600 at 19px for features, Newsreader 25px for audiences, Inter 26px for pricing names. Desktop also jumps straight from an 80px H2 to a 19px H3 with no step between.
The blue rule under 'hookworthy.' runs through the italic y's descender.
The two-tone white/grey H2 couplet is used 9 times, so it turns into a habit. Sixteen to 28 labels sit at 10.5 to 11.5px.
typefully-a.fix: On phones, drop the H2s to about 32px (keep the H1 at 43px, which already fills the width in 2 lines) so the ratio is at least 1.35. Use one H3 family throughout (Newsreader 25px), and move the underline below the descender or knock it out around the y.

arc-b.verdict: The most typographic idea in the set: the type itself shows the before and after. But the hero headline is crushed.
arc-b.loved: Assigning meaning to faces: the soft line is Instrument Serif italic with strikes, the sharp line is heavy Bricolage on lime, and the receipt is Geist Mono. You read the edit before you read the words, and the final CTA's struck italic 'so i think, honestly, just, lol' above the headline pays it off.
problems: The H1 stacks three kinds of tightening on Bricolage: width 78%, weight 800 and -0.036em tracking. In 'Good ideas die' the letters touch and the counters of e/a/o clog.
The 'sharp' first line is about 585px wide while the 'soft' italic line is about 790px and set larger (120 vs 111px). The soft voice wins visually, which inverts the message.
The grotesk-line-plus-italic-line formula repeats in about 17 H2s and H3s, and Bricolage plus Instrument Serif is the 2024 indie-SaaS default pairing.
Instrument Serif italic with strikes at 14 to 20px (the soft drafts in the tiles) has a tiny x-height and is hard to read. 16 mono labels are at 11.5px.
arc-b.fix: Set the display Bricolage at width 100 with -0.015em tracking (or width 85 with 0 tracking), and size line 1 to match line 2's measure so the sharp voice is the louder one.

arc-a.verdict: The house system set cleanly on a blue stage. Assured on desktop, timid on the phone.
arc-a.loved: The centred Newsreader 380 H1 at 105px on ultramarine: an inverted-pyramid two-liner with good optical sizing, hairlines that hold on the saturated blue, and the amber squiggle under 'first lines.' Before text is grey Inter and after text is white Newsreader, the right semantic split.
problems: The phone H1 is only 41px and fills about 260 of 358px. With H2s at 37px and the card's post text at 24px, the hero barely leads.
Below the hero, 81% of characters are Inter at 13 to 15px, so the lower page reads as generic dark SaaS rather than editorial.
The green inserted capitals ('M', 'S') in the hero card leave a visible gap before 'Most'.
H3 family is inconsistent (Newsreader 32px features, Inter 17/600 audiences). 12 of 60 paragraphs end in a one-word widow on phone.
arc-a.fix: Set the phone H1 to about 52px with clamp() (it still fits in 2 lines) and the H2s to about 32px, and add text-wrap: pretty to body copy.

awwwards-b.verdict: The best headline idea in the round, buried under a mono-and-handwriting habit.
awwwards-b.loved: 'Write it rough.' in grey Geist Mono 300 over 'Post it sharp.' in EB Garamond 500 at 158px with a swash italic 'sharp.' The typewriter-to-typeset contrast is the whole product in one line. The roman/italic H2 couplets ('Your facts stay. / The fluff goes.') are proper editorial setting, and the prices use lining figures.
problems: Four faces, and the mono has no single job. Geist Mono is 27% of all characters, with 61 uppercase tracked leaves (nav, buttons, labels, footer), so it no longer signals 'draft'.
Caveat (the stock handwriting face) carries the most important words on the page: the move, 'Led with the number.'
There are 36 text items at 11px and 7 at 10px, mostly uppercase mono on beige. Galley mono runs at a 3.0 line-height with Caveat insertions colliding into the words (the churn card).
EB Garamond is a text cut: at 158px its low contrast reads soft. Desktop H3s have one-word widows ('...minus the / shill.', '...turned into a / post.'), and the final CTA at 130px rivals the H1.
awwwards-b.fix: Keep Geist Mono for the rough draft and the counts only. Set the nav, buttons and labels in Inter at 13px or more in sentence case, and set the move line in Garamond italic in blue pencil instead of Caveat.

apple-b.verdict: Competent Apple-tight Inter that gives a writing product no typographic voice.
apple-b.loved: It uses Inter's real optical-size axis (opsz 32, verified in the font) at 680 weight and 130px with 0.93 leading. 'Write the line / they stop for.' is tightly built and fills the phone width at 56px without breaking the 2-line rule.
problems: 99% of the text is Inter. Soft vs sharp and before vs after are carried only by colour and strikethrough, never by type, on a page about writing.
Nine H2s in identical 85px bold with no tonal or italic contrast, so every section shouts at the same volume. 'Premium / 500 / 500K' in display bold competes with them.
The -0.052em tracking is applied unchanged at 56px on phone, and opsz 32 display spacing is forced onto 18 to 22px H3s and pricing names.
The desktop hero lede is about 24 characters per line. The decorative feed sets thousands of characters at 13.5px behind the hero card, and the struck old line is cut off with 'af…'.
apple-b.fix: Bring a second voice back: set the sharpened post line and the second line of each H2 in Newsreader (or at least a lighter weight). Loosen tracking as size drops (about -0.03em at 44 to 56px) and let opsz run automatically on the small headings.

pickWhy: It's the only design where each face has one job: Newsreader for your words and headlines, Inter for interface and network chrome, Geist Mono for times and counts. Its hero is the most finely set headline in the round. Its faults are a flat phone scale and inconsistent H3s, which take an afternoon of CSS. The others need structural type changes.
combo: Keep typefully-a's system and hero, but replace its grey two-tone H2 couplets with awwwards-b's roman/italic couplets. Then borrow arc-b's idea that the type performs the edit: the soft draft in light Newsreader italic with the amber squiggle, the sharp line in heavier Newsreader roman.
